method: Second check by another method (review.py): for each representative point, the scan column at that angle is read against the printed gridlines next to it, with no rectification and no frame calibration of values. The approximate value by eye only picks the run to read. Each point is compared with the nearest extracted sample.
operator: Claude (AI agent), Firstmate crewmate run for the site owner

units_and_conventions.ordinate: MAGNITUDE IN DB, linear, -70.0 to -10.0 at the frame edges, gridlines every 10.0
units_and_conventions.abscissa: ANGLE IN DEGREES, linear, 175 to 185 at the frame edges, gridlines every 1
units_and_conventions.angle_convention: phi = 180 degrees when the nose points toward the radar (section 5.1)
units_and_conventions.traces: solid = reconstructed, dotted = original, as each caption states

tolerance.rule: A point passes when the two values differ by no more than the larger of 0.6 dB and the sample's own extraction error.

points.note: Corrected eye value. The first reading by eye, -37.4 dB, was wrong.

clipped.note: The solid line reaches the -70 dB frame. The extraction must show a gap here, not a value.

eye_reading_note: One reading by eye was wrong: fig-5-11 at 180.24 degrees, read as -37.4 dB. The column measurement gives -41.4 dB, between the printed -40 and -50 gridlines at rows 483 and 622.
